learn: The elements (line, shape, form, value, colour, space, texture) are the vocabulary of visual art.
The principles (balance, contrast, emphasis, movement, pattern, rhythm, proportion, unity, variety) are its grammar.
High school art asks you to use them deliberately to communicate an idea.
check: The elements are the visual art's...
High school art uses elements and principles...
lessons.try: Make a one-page visual glossary of all elements and principles.

learn: Formal analysis describes how elements and principles create the work's effect.
Begin with first impressions, then describe, then analyse relationships.
Use precise vocabulary: "diagonal lines create movement toward the focal point."
lessons.try: Write a formal analysis of a painting from before 1930.

learn: A concept is the idea behind a work.
Artists choose media, scale and style to support their concept.
Intent guides decisions from sketches to final piece.
check: A concept is the ___ behind a work.
lessons.try: Write a concept statement for a new work and three supporting choices.

learn: Line quality varies weight, thickness and pressure to suggest form and depth.
Contour lines define edges; cross-contour lines wrap around forms.
Heavier lines can bring edges forward.
lessons.try: Draw a shell using varied line weight and cross-contours.

learn: Use sighting, angles and negative space to check proportions.
Block in large shapes before details.
Compare relationships constantly: "the handle is half the cup's height."
lessons.try: Draw a complex object using sighting and blocking in.

learn: Gesture drawing captures action and weight in seconds.
Proportions of the adult figure: about seven and a half heads tall.
Draw from clothed models and from your own observations in public places.
check: An adult is about ___ heads tall.
lessons.try: Fill a page with 30-second gesture drawings.

learn: A strong value structure reads clearly even in a small thumbnail.
Limit values to three to five in planning sketches.
Squint to simplify what you see.
lessons.try: Make three-value thumbnail studies of a landscape.

learn: Form shadows are on the object; cast shadows fall onto other surfaces.
Core shadows mark the turning point from light to dark.
Edges can be hard or soft depending on form and light.
check: The darkest part of the form shadow is the...
lessons.try: Draw a white object lit from one side.

learn: Graphite, charcoal, ink wash and conté each create value differently.
Charcoal makes rich darks and can be erased to make lights.
Ink wash uses diluted ink in layers.
check: Lights can be made in charcoal by...
lessons.try: Draw the same object in charcoal and ink wash.

learn: Every colour has hue (name), value (lightness) and saturation (intensity).
Saturated colours are vivid; desaturated colours are muted.
Value matters more than hue for readability.
lessons.try: Paint a colour study and a matching greyscale value study.

learn: Harmonies include complementary, analogous, triadic, split-complementary and tetradic.
A dominant colour with accents creates unity.
Colour temperature creates depth: warm advances, cool recedes.
check: A split-complementary scheme uses a colour and the two ___ its complement.
lessons.try: Paint a landscape in a split-complementary scheme.

learn: Colour meanings vary by culture: white means purity in some cultures and mourning in others.
Artists use colour symbolically and emotionally.
Pablo Picasso's Blue Period (1901-1904) used blue to express sorrow.
lessons.try: Create two versions of a scene with different emotional colour.

learn: Techniques: flat wash, graded wash, wet-on-wet, dry brush, lifting.
Plan whites in advance; paint light to dark.
Winslow Homer painted luminous watercolours in the late 1800s.
lessons.try: Paint a sky with a graded wash.

learn: Acrylic dries fast and can be layered; oil dries slowly and blends smoothly.
Fat over lean: in oils, each layer should have more oil than the one below.
Glazing uses thin transparent layers; impasto uses thick paint.
lessons.try: Paint a small study using glazing.

learn: Plan with thumbnails; decide focal point and value structure.
Block in big shapes, then refine.
Step back often to see the whole.
check: Painters should step back to see the...
lessons.try: Complete a painting from thumbnail to finished work.

learn: Relief: carve away non-printing areas (linocut, woodcut).
Intaglio: ink lines cut below the surface (etching, drypoint).
Albrecht Dürer (1471-1528) was a master of both.
check: In relief printing you carve away...
lessons.try: Make a linocut with a clear positive and negative design.

learn: Pattern repeats motifs in regular arrangements.
Tessellations fit shapes together without gaps.
Islamic geometric art creates complex patterns from simple shapes.
check: Shapes that fit without gaps form a...
Islamic geometric art builds patterns from...
lessons.try: Design a repeating pattern tile and print it four times.

learn: An edition is a numbered set of identical prints: 3/10 means the third of ten.
An artist's proof (A/P) is a test print.
Sign prints in pencil below the image.
lessons.try: Print and number a small edition.

learn: Additive (modelling, assembling), subtractive (carving) and casting (pouring material into a mould).
Auguste Rodin's "The Thinker" (1904 cast) is a famous bronze.
Scale and viewpoint change a sculpture's impact.
check: Pouring material into a mould is...
lessons.try: Model a small figure in clay showing a clear gesture.

learn: Hand-building methods: pinch, coil and slab; wheel-throwing uses a potter's wheel.
Clay is fired in a kiln to harden it; glazes add colour and seal surfaces.
Join clay with score and slip.
check: Clay is hardened by firing in a...
lessons.try: Build a coil vessel with a decorative surface.

learn: Installations transform a space that viewers enter.
Site-specific art responds to a particular location.
Viewers' movement becomes part of the experience.
lessons.try: Design an installation for a corner of your school.

learn: Exposure depends on aperture, shutter speed and ISO.
Fast shutter freezes motion; slow shutter blurs it.
Wide aperture (small f-number) blurs backgrounds.
check: Exposure depends on aperture, shutter and...
lessons.try: Photograph the same scene with fast and slow shutter speeds.

learn: Rule of thirds, leading lines, framing, symmetry and point of view.
Changing angle (low, high) changes meaning.
Light quality: golden hour light is warm and soft.
check: A low angle can make subjects look...
lessons.try: Take a series of ten photos on one theme.

learn: Editing adjusts exposure, contrast, colour and cropping.
Layers and masks allow non-destructive edits.
Manipulating news photos to deceive is unethical; disclose major edits.
check: Deceptive manipulation of news photos is...
lessons.try: Edit a photo and write a note on the changes made.

learn: Prehistoric cave art, Egyptian tomb painting, Greek sculpture and Roman mosaics.
Medieval art included Byzantine icons, Islamic calligraphy and Gothic cathedrals.
Art served religion, power and memory.
lessons.try: Make a visual timeline from prehistory to 1400.

learn: Renaissance artists (Leonardo, Michelangelo, Raphael) used perspective and anatomy.
Baroque art (Caravaggio, Rembrandt) used drama and light.
Romanticism and Realism in the 1800s explored emotion and everyday life.
lessons.try: Compare a Renaissance and a Baroque painting.

learn: Japanese ukiyo-e prints influenced European Impressionists.
African sculpture influenced Picasso and early modernists.
Modern art (Impressionism to Abstract Expressionism) questioned what art could be.
lessons.try: Research one global influence on modern art.

learn: Critique structure: describe, analyse, interpret, evaluate.
Give feedback that is specific, actionable and kind.
Receive feedback with openness and ask clarifying questions.
lessons.try: Participate in a group critique and record feedback.

learn: Reflect on process, challenges and growth.
An artist statement explains concept, process and influences.
Write clearly and avoid jargon.
lessons.try: Write a 150-word artist statement for your strongest piece.

learn: Select 10-15 strong works showing range and growth.
Photograph work well: even light, square angles, neutral background.
Order the portfolio to tell a story.
lessons.try: Photograph and assemble a digital portfolio.
